ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows an operational amplifier voltage comparator. The non-inverting input terminal “+” of the operational amplifier is directly grounded; the inverting input terminal “-” is connected to a node, and this node is connected respectively through two resistors labeled 10 kΩ to -3 V and the input voltage ui. The output terminal of the operational amplifier is connected through resistor R to the output uo, and the output node also has a voltage-regulator diode VDZ connected to ground, with the regulated value ±UZ = ±6 V marked in the figure. Then reason: the threshold voltage of the comparator occurs when the potentials of the two input terminals are equal. Because the non-inverting terminal is grounded, at the threshold V+ = 0 V, so V− must be 0 V. The inverting-terminal node is divided/averaged from ui and -3 V through two equal 10 kΩ resistors, and the ideal operational amplifier input current is approximately 0, therefore V− = (ui + (-3 V))/2. Let V− = 0, obtaining (ui - 3 V)/2 = 0, so ui = 3 V. Therefore the threshold voltage of the circuit UT = 3 V.

method.method_draft: First identify the comparator inputs in the image: V+ is tied to ground, and V− is fed through two equal 10 kΩ resistors from −3 V and ui. At the threshold, V− = V+ = 0 V. Because the two resistors are equal and the op-amp input draws negligible current, V− = (ui + (−3 V))/2. Set this equal to 0 and solve ui = 3 V, so the threshold voltage UT is 3 V.

method.method_draft: Let the voltage at the inverting input node be v−. From the image, the two currents through the equal 10 kΩ resistors are (v− − (−3))/10k and (v− − ui)/10k. At the switching threshold, the grounded non-inverting input gives v− = 0. Apply KCL at the high-impedance inverting node: (0 + 3)/10k + (0 − ui)/10k = 0. Solving gives ui = 3 V, hence UT = 3 V. The stated UZ = 6 V only fixes the output clamp level and is not used in the threshold equation.
